title: Privacy Card
description: A structured artefact capturing the privacy architecture of a PET-protected system, dataset, model, pipeline, or query service. Schema 2.0 (breaking change from 1.2) adds: (i) structured evidence references with explicit evidence_class enum [Duddu et al. CODASPY 2025, §3; IBM Atlas arXiv:2502.19567, §4 — the verifiable-card and in-toto provenance lineage]; (ii) device_class on PET components for CPS/IoT deployments [Mo et al. MobiSys 2020 §5; Gupta et al. arXiv:2511.00037 §4]; (iii) trust_zone on stepwise steps [aligned with NIST 1500-201 CPS reference architecture]; (iv) cps_subject_type on deployment context; (v) explicit threat_profile in risk_calibration [Boenisch et al. EuroS&P 2023 §5 — the honest-but-curious to malicious-server shift changes ε* by ≈2×]; (vi) refactored risk_calibration with three first-class ε quantities — design target, accountant, empirical-audit lower bound [Steinke, Nasr, Jagielski NeurIPS 2023; Kulynych et al. NeurIPS 2024 §3]. All explorer cross-references (primitive_id, pairing_ref, stack_ref, sector_ref) must match IDs in the T1–T4 tables. See MIGRATION_NOTES.md for the 1.2 → 2.0 diff.

evidence_reference.description: A reference to an evidence artefact (result record, attestation, audit log, signed receipt). Made structured in 2.0 so the evidence_class is always declared. Evidence-class taxonomy follows the verifiable-card lineage [Duddu et al. CODASPY 2025 (Laminator) §3; IBM Atlas arXiv:2502.19567 §4; Guo et al. arXiv:2412.10537 (VerifiableFL) §3].

location.description: Path, URI, or content-addressable identifier pointing to the evidence artefact.

evidence_class.description: What kind of evidence this is. The hierarchy is monotonic in tamper-resistance: (a) `reproducible-record` — the metric is reproducible from the audit-trailed config + seed + dataset hash, but the record itself is not cryptographically signed; sufficient for internal reproducibility, insufficient as dispute evidence (this is the typical state of an ML result record committed to a repo). (b) `signed-record` — the record (or its hash) is signed by the producing party with a verifiable key (e.g. JWS over a Solid consent receipt via WebID-DPoP), giving non-repudiation against the producer alone. (c) `countersigned-record` — additionally signed by a second party with an independent key (a witness, audit body, or institutional counterparty), giving non-repudiation across two trust domains. (d) `hash-chain-committed` — committed to an append-only log with periodic external anchors (in-toto-style, Atlas 2025 §4). (e) `notarised` — additionally anchored to a public ledger or notary service offering third-party attestation of time-of-commit. Workshop attendees should always be able to answer: which evidence-class does each `evidence_ref` warrant, given the dispute scenario it would be invoked in? (see workshops/W2-card-construction.md).

produced_by.description: Identity (WebID, DID, or institutional identifier) of the party producing this evidence. Required for evidence_class ∈ {signed-record, countersigned-record, hash-chain-committed, notarised}.

countersigned_by.description: Identities of additional signing parties. Required for evidence_class ∈ {countersigned-record, notarised}.

anchor_log.description: URI of the append-only log or notary service this evidence is anchored to. Required for evidence_class ∈ {hash-chain-committed, notarised}.

device_class.description: Device class for CPS/IoT deployments. Two FL deployments with identical (ε, δ) can offer materially different actual privacy depending on which devices participated and what each one's trust profile is. Vocabulary motivated by Gupta et al. arXiv:2511.00037 §4 (FL framework benchmarking across device assumptions) and Mo et al. MobiSys 2020 §5 (DarkneTZ — discriminating between TEE classes at the edge).

trust_zone.description: Trust zone the step operates in. Aligned with the NIST 1500-201 CPS reference architecture layers. `enclave` denotes operation inside a TEE substrate; `off-platform` denotes anything terminating outside the deployment's trust boundary (e.g. a third-party witness service).

threat_profile.description: Adversary model the deployment is calibrated against. The honest-but-curious / malicious-server distinction is load-bearing: Boenisch et al. EuroS&P 2023 §5 show that the operationally meaningful ε* shifts by ≈2× when moving from honest-but-curious to malicious-server. Required in risk_calibration because every empirical attack-rate quoted on a card is calibrated against exactly one profile, and conflating them is the most common over-reading of FL privacy claims [Carlini et al. S&P 2022 §6; Boenisch et al. EuroS&P 2023 §5].

cps_subject_type.description: The CPS/IoT subject role on whose behalf the privacy claim is being made. Affects the natural unit of disclosure (record vs subject vs cohort) and therefore which MIA variant is the operationally relevant one [Suri et al. PoPETs 2023 §3 — subject-level MIA in cross-silo FL].

card_id.description: Unique identifier for this card. Suggested format: CARD-{slug}-{YYYYMM}.

schema_version.description: Schema version this card was written against. 2.0 is a breaking change from 1.2; see MIGRATION_NOTES.md. 1.2 added the optional `risk_calibration` block for operational DP reporting. 1.1 added stepwise_chain, exposure_problem_refs, jurisdictional_context. 1.0 cards remain valid under their original schema but should be migrated for new work.

title.description: Short human-readable name for this privacy architecture.

description.description: One or two sentences describing what this card represents.

created.description: ISO 8601 date this card was first created.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 date this card was last materially revised.

authors.description: Individuals or teams responsible for this card.

architecture_pattern.description: References back to the T2/T3 explorer tables for the combination pattern this card instantiates.

custom.description: Set true if this card represents a combination not yet registered in T2/T3.

custom_rationale.description: If custom=true, explain why this combination is not in the explorer tables.

pet_components.description: The PET primitives present in this architecture, in order of application.

primitive_id.description: T1 primitive ID. DP retained as family pointer; prefer DP-L or DP-C for explicit trust model. SDC (classical statistical disclosure control — coarsening & suppression) is a legacy technique, not a modern PET; it is included in this enum for cards that need to model it, but see GLOSSARY.md §4 and data/primitives.yaml for why it does not fit the 'algorithmic PET' definition cleanly.

role.description: What this primitive contributes to the overall architecture.

implementation_status.description: Current implementation status of this component.

device_class.description: Device class hosting this PET component, where applicable. New in 2.0.

tooling.description: Specific frameworks, libraries, or products implementing this primitive.

parameters.description: Key configuration parameters for this primitive. Schema is open-ended; document what is material for assurance.

parameter_notes.description: Narrative on parameter choices, constraints, or known governance gaps.

attestation_evidence.description: Attestation receipt for this PET component, where applicable (e.g. TEE attestation document). Required for primitive_id=TEE in schema 2.0 if implementation_status=deployed; see CPSDEV-ATTEST-001 rule.

trust_model.description: Who is trusted, what they are trusted with, and where trust breaks down.

summary.description: Narrative description of the overall trust model.

threat_actors.description: Entities considered in the threat model.

out_of_scope_threats.description: Threats explicitly not covered by this architecture.

assurance_targets.description: The assurance artefacts this deployment commits to producing.

required_artefacts.description: Artefacts that must exist for this architecture to be considered deployment-ready. In 2.0, the `evidence` block is structured (uses evidence_reference) — `location` alone is insufficient because the reviewer needs to know what kind of evidence is on offer.

evidence.description: Structured evidence reference. Required if status=exists. New in 2.0; replaces the bare `location` string from 1.2.

current_maturity_stage.description: Self-assessed maturity stage (1–4) per the explorer rubric.

maturity_justification.description: Why this maturity stage was assigned.

governance_controls.description: Procedural and institutional controls in place or planned.

deployment_context.description: The operational and regulatory context in which this architecture is deployed.

cps_subject_type.description: The CPS/IoT subject role this card's privacy claims protect. New in 2.0. Required for cards in CPS/IoT settings; affects the natural unit of disclosure and therefore which MIA variant is operationally relevant [Suri et al. PoPETs 2023 §3].

data_subjects_jurisdiction.description: Jurisdictions whose data protection law applies.

regulatory_context.description: Regulatory requirements and alignment gaps for this deployment.

data_profile_ref.description: Path or URI to a Data Profile document associated with this card.

tooling_candidates.description: Open-source or commercial tools evaluated or in use for this architecture.

residual_risks.description: Known risks not addressed by the current architecture.

utility_evidence.description: Evidence that the architecture preserves sufficient utility for its intended purpose.

risk_calibration.description: Operational reporting of the deployment's DP claim. Refactored in 2.0 to make the three operationally distinct ε quantities first-class: design target (what the deployment promises), accountant (what composition bounds), empirical-audit (what an audit can falsify). Reporting only one mis-leads reviewers about which assurance is actually on offer [Desfontaines blog 2023; Kulynych et al. NeurIPS 2024 §3 — the f-DP-to-attack-rate mapping the target_advantage field instantiates; Steinke, Nasr, Jagielski NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper — one-run empirical lower bound]. The `threat_profile` is now required because every quantity below is calibrated against exactly one profile, and conflating profiles is the most common over-reading [Boenisch et al. EuroS&P 2023 §5].

threat_profile.description: Adversary model these quantities are calibrated against.

design_target.description: What the deployment promises. The aspirational privacy claim before any empirical measurement.

mu_dp.description: Gaussian-DP μ parameter [Dong, Roth, Su JRSS-B 2022].

attack_target.description: Stated attack the design target is calibrated against [Kulynych et al. NeurIPS 2024].

accountant.description: What composition bounds. Output of the DP accountant under the configured (σ, T, q, δ).

rdp_envelope.description: ε under a single-α Rényi-DP envelope [Mironov CSF 2017].

prv.description: ε under the PRV accountant [Gopi, Lee, Wutschitz NeurIPS 2021] — the tighter modern accountant for FL composition.

mu_dp.description: μ-DP composition result [Dong, Roth, Su JRSS-B 2022].

evidence.description: Pointer to the accountant log establishing these values.

empirical_audit.description: What an audit can falsify. The empirical ε lower bound from canary-based DP auditing [Jagielski, Ullman, Oprea NeurIPS 2020; Nasr et al. USENIX Security 2023; Steinke, Nasr, Jagielski NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper — one-run auditing recommended].

method.description: Auditing technique. 'canife' = FL-specific crafted canaries [Maddock et al. ICLR 2023]. 'canary-one-run' = single-training-run multi-canary audit [Steinke, Nasr, Jagielski NeurIPS 2023].

epsilon_lower_bound.description: Clopper-Pearson lower bound on empirical ε. Zero means the audit at this scale cannot falsify the design target.

evidence.description: Pointer to the canary-audit result record.

measured_advantage.description: Empirically measured adversary advantage under attack(s) actually mounted against the released model.

trade_off_curve.description: Reference to the FPR-vs-FNR curve data or plot for this calibration.

stepwise_chain.description: Stepwise-from-private construction (see STEPWISE_RISK.md). Each entry records one deviation from the completely-private baseline (step 0).

trust_zone.description: Trust zone this step operates in. New in 2.0.

evidence_anchor.description: Structured evidence reference backing this step's assurance claim. New in 2.0 (the textual `assurance_anchor` is kept for narrative; this is the machine-checkable pointer).
